Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

score 0.29expressions of optimism or emphasis, especially in agreement, impact, or condition
expressions of optimism or emphasis; tokens like "and," "so," and ",", especially in contexts of agreement, impact, or condition.
L6·N632unmasked layer
This neuron tracks the predicate slot in a consequence clause introduced by "so": it fires positively on affirmative continuation tokens there (e.g., "is", "in", "now", "and", "signed", the comma after "checked it out"), and is strongly *suppressed* when that slot is filled by a negation/hedge ("not", "may", "little").

Fires on the continuation/completing sub-word piece of a multi-token rare proper name (surname, brand, or place name), especially when it appears at the very start of a document — e.g. "dorf" in Reins|dorf, "ov" in Filat|ov, "ack" in Ball|ack, "ion" in Pel|ion, " Beach" in Boynton| Beach; suppressed on ordinary mid-text function words/punctuation.

L6·N1970unmasked layer
This neuron is essentially a weak, signed detector on word-internal continuation pieces of names/abbreviations: it fires slightly positively on subword fragments completing proper nouns, acronyms or specialized noun heads ("​.S" in "U.S", "strom" in "Borgstrom", "Kot" in "Kotzebue", the "1" in "F1 Visa", " loan", " programme"), and is very strongly suppressed on capitalized/CamelCase fragments finishing an acronym or place name ("TO" in "TORONTO", "VO" in "OVO", "OS" in "triOS", "ow" in "Thurlow").

L6·N4311unmasked layer

Both extremes land on word-internal sub-word fragments of rare proper nouns/technical strings (e.g. Oracle I|LOM, mael|strom, SAM|D12, S|OD|IUM, Fog Lin|en; suppressed by L|agn|ado, Kap|ach, Beg|uel|in), so it is essentially a position-based detector of continuation pieces inside unusual capitalized names rather than a semantic feature — positive for product/technical tokens, strongly negative for personal-name fragments.

L6·N5834unmasked layer
Poorly selective, low-magnitude neuron: its top activations are on ordinary mid-sentence function words (" part", " the", " such") and on word-initial sub-word fragments that begin a longer multi-token word (" se"|awater, "-inst"|alled, " Ann"|alise), while very similar tokens in other contexts (" there", "-t"ails, "Res"idential, " Se"uss) drive it strongly negative — i.e. it tracks fine-grained token/continuation context rather than any coherent concept.
